Question: I recently had a growth talk with my manager. He is pleased with my performance but said that I can come off as a know-it-all sometimes. What are some actionable steps I can take to improve my behavior?
Answer: Listen to people around you. Repeat what you've heard in your own words to demonstrate you heard. Experiment a bit by trying their suggestion. Talk with them again about the parts of their suggestion that worked. You're surrounded by people with more experience than you. For example yesterday I was talking to an engineer at least ten years younger than me, I'd solved similar problems before and he hadn't so I was feeling pretty confident. Then I realised he had far more relevant experience than me with a couple key specifics. Together we came up with a much better solution than I would have on my own. Nobody likes working with a know-it-all. People do like working with a competent colleague. The difference is easy to articulate but hard to sustain.

Question: How do you get a 20,000% increment in your salary in the last 25 years?
Answer: We say that an increase in salary from $20,000 to $40,000 is fundamentally different to an increase from $120,000 to $140,000 and you really need to use percentages. This question highlights the need for two further rules: Percentages start to become unwieldy at 100%. A 20000% salary increase is close enough to multiplying salary by 200. With three numbers rather than five it's considerably easier to understand. The second rule is that any time period over about five years should be adjusted for inflation or else the reader is left trying to work out whether the percentage increase is meaningless. We know the normal range of salaries is say $20,000 to $200,000. There are people outside this at both extremes, but for practical purposes the point is that salary can only increase by 10x. Any more and you are talking about something with such an extreme that the insanely high or low salary is the interesting story rather than the change over time.

Question: Okay I know I’m a bit young to think about this but I’m 15 and I turn 18 in 3 years. How will I work and make a small amount of money in a month and find a house and still pay rent, do I look for a cheap house?

Question: What percentage should I earn if a friend is investing into my business idea with $100,000? I will be the one managing the entire business, just that it’s my idea and a friend’s money.
Answer: How much would you earn if you got a job on the open market? How much will you earn in this venture (outside any percentage share). That difference is your investment in the business. Compare that to the amount your friend invested ($100k) to get the percentage split.

Question: Do people have to pay to have electric cars charged?
Answer: Where I live, the cost of electricity between 11pm and 6am is so low that it's effectively free. Power plants can optimise their output for peak times but they can't be shut down entirely, so much of this overnight power is wasted Those seven hours of extremely cheap electricity are enough to charge my car 70 miles. So provided I didn't drive more than 70 in the previous day I can refill essentially for free. If course there is no such thing as free electricity. It's currently a waste product because supply exceeds demand but that will change as EV adoption grows. I've also been toying with buying batteries for the house that I charge overnight but haven't because I expect the bargain price to be gone in a few years.
